doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Playing with Grady Tate and Christian McBride, and Jazz Nativity
summary: Roy's pleasure with the rhythm section and a joke by Grady Tate; Grady joins them yearly at Jazz Nativity.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: And for me it was a great pleasure working with Grady Tate on drums.

And I really loved Christian’s playing. And he’s such a big, warm guy, like he just gives you hugs and says, “yeah, it was good playing with you again.” And with Grady, after we finished, I’m going to tell you this and you can cut it if you like, I went over to him, we went down to the dressing room and I put my arm around him and says, “Grady, it was just wonderful, because playing with you is really a comfort.” And he says “yeah, like a jock strap.”

We know him pretty well because he does the Jazz Nativity with us every year. We’ve been doing that thing for eight, nine years. And this year he sings the opening song. He’s a wonderful singer, as you know. And then of course we see him every year at that, and so we’re always in the same dressing room. Everybody’s in the one dressing room, and there’s a lot of jokes, and that’s one of the things we enjoy about doing that is because we get to hang out with the musicians every year.
